messages:
Marta C: Quick follow-up on the routing-policy RFC. I sketched a smaller-surface refactor: evaluate policies as a declarative DAG (matches -> score nodes -> penalties -> combiner) and provide a thin runtime fastpath hook that can return top-K without materializing or sorting full outputs. Thoughts?

Ravi Patel: Dig the DAG. Two immediate Qs: 1) preemption windows (reserved vs best-effort) - model as hard-blocks or penalties? 2) perf hit - will an extra graph layer add per-request CPU we cant afford?

Alice Ng: For preemption, model as a time-aware penalty node that can produce a block flag. Keeps scorer contract simple: either numeric score or block. On perf: compile hot subgraphs into an optimized in-memory form and cache per policy_version; that should keep p99s low.

Sam Ortiz: Agree keep tie-breaker in runtime (hash(request_id + tenant_salt)). If graph emits equal scores, runtime handles tie deterministically. Avoids encoding randomness in policies.

Priya Rao: Also add stable bucketization (deterministic salt + consistent hashing) to avoid route flip-flop across retries/replicas.

Marta C: Interface proposal: graph_eval -> list of {route_id, score, flags} -> runtime sorts + tie-breaker + capacity checks + preemption enforcement. Fastpath: runtime callback for approximate topK to avoid full sort on cold paths.

Ravi Patel: Implementation note: graph nodes must be pure (no side-effects). If a node needs telemetry, it emits a lightweight tag; runtime maps tags to metrics. No policy code should call metrics APIs directly.

Alice Ng: Example policy snippet (YAML):
```yaml
policy_version: v2
nodes:
  - id: geo_match
    type: match
    expr: region == request.region
  - id: latency_penalty
    type: penalty
    expr: max(0, (p50 - target_p50) * 0.1)
  - id: final_score
    type: combine
    inputs: [geo_match, latency_penalty, cost_weight]
```
Runtime receives: `[{route: r1, score: 0.72, flags: []}, ...]`.

Sam Ortiz: Fastpath idea: expose a C API that, given a precompiled graph and candidate routes, returns topK using branch-and-bound heuristics. Benchmarks for 10/100/1000 route sets will determine threshold.

Priya Rao: Telemetry wishlist:
- policy_decision.count (per policy_version)
- policy_node.duration_ms histogram (per node_id)
- policy_routed.topk_latency_ms
- policy_fallback.count + reason tag
Also emit percentiles for decisions >1ms and tag with policy_version and route_bucket.

Marta C: Rollout plan: 1) static linter + unit tests, 2) dry-run in sandbox (shadow exec) 48h, 3) 5% canary (route-level) with telemetry gates, 4) 25% canary + runbook signoff, 5) full cutover. Auto-rollback on error_rate_up or p99_latency regress beyond configured delta.

Ravi Patel: How will SEs preview changes? Need policy diff/preview in console that shows how new/old graphs score a sample request with a trace. Without that, authoring is blind.

Alice Ng: Console preview doable. We'll support side-by-side evaluation of sample requests against old and new graphs. Need a synthetic request generator for corner cases and extreme tenants.

infra-bot: deploy-plan created: `plans/1749002468/policy-graph/lightweight-hooks` (owner: Marta C) :gear:

Sam Ortiz: Tests: add property tests that mutate tenancy, region, and load to validate fallthroughs. Add chaos tests for partial capacity loss, preemption flips, and node exceptions.

Priya Rao: Ops invariant: if runtime returns `block_by_policy`, log one structured line with {policy_version, node_id, reason}. That makes customer-reject debugging much faster.

Marta C: Ownership: I'll own graph shape and console preview. Ravi owns runtime hook API + perf microbenchmarks. Alice owns linting + policy compiler. Sam owns canary infra & tests. Priya owns telemetry + rollback rules.

Ravi Patel: Timeline: 3w design + prototype, 2w sandbox + tests, 1w canary = approx 6 weeks. Can we commit?

Alice Ng: Yep. Small ask: include a YAML -> compiled binary cache schema for fast runtime loads.

Priya Rao: Add SLOs for policy-eval: p50 < 0.2ms, p99 < 2ms in hot cache. Set alerts on shifts and increased variance.

Marta C: Next steps: I'll update the RFC with graph spec and interface stubs. Ravi drop initial API sketch in #eng-runtime by EOD. Sam create sandbox runbook. Thanks all :raised_hands:
